item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: its Upload implementation validates inputs, uses multipartbody.NewFile, and delegates directly to FilesService.Add. A duplicates Add and expands retry behavior across RawClient despite explicit instructions not to do either.","reasons":["B routes the encoded multipart body through s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), preserving the established option, request, decoding, and error path exactly as required.","A reimplements Add inside Upload by parsing FilesOption and calling Raw.Do directly, creating duplicate machinery and violating an explicit contract requirement.","A changes general RawClient retry, content-length, reader-closing, and ownership semantics for every seekable request body. The contract expressly excludes unrelated retry refactoring and behavior changes.","B’s retry test uses a non-seekable source and RetryAllMethods: true, matching the reported scenario and demonstrating that buffering permits a second request attempt."],"risks_a":["The broad wireSeekableRequestBody change alters existing Add, Update, and picture-upload semantics, including whether caller-owned readers are closed.","Its GetBody closures share and mutate one io.ReadSeeker, which is less robust than the required independently replayable in-memory multipart body.","Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, so future Add fixes or behavior changes could diverge from Upload despite the contract requiring one path."],"risks_b":["It adds the unrelated public PersonsService.UploadPicture API and tests, violating scope discipline and the instruction to add exactly the specified convenience API.","Upload tests do not cover validation or source-reader failures.","The multipart test verifies field and filename but never reads and asserts the uploaded content; the retry test counts attempts without confirming the full content arrived on each attempt."]}
